I've looped in Dev (legal ops), Marcus (account lead), and Olga (security). Proposed plan:

Team / Ellen —

I reviewed Maple's 24-hour notice ask. Operationally, time-to-detect varies and we need time to validate events before sending a customer notification. Proposed compromise:
- Initial notification: Redwood will provide an initial notification within 72 hours of determining that an incident has occurred that materially affects customer data. The notice will include a high-level description, impacted data classes, and immediate mitigations.
- Confirmed incident follow-up: Redwood will provide a detailed incident report (including evidence and root-cause where available) within 14 days for confirmed incidents; for incidents requiring forensic analysis, we'll provide interim updates every 5 business days until final report.
- Cooperation: Redwood will use reasonable efforts to provide requested evidence and support in accordance with agreed escalation contacts and will aim to deliver non-privileged evidence within 10 business days of a formal request. If Maple requests forensic images or raw logs that fall outside normal operational retention, costs and legal approvals may apply.

On subprocessors: we can offer a 30-day advance notice for new subprocessors and a 15-day objection window for high-risk categories (payments, identity providers); objections should be raised to security@redwood.com with justification.

I'll attach suggested tracked changes to the DPA with the above language. If Maple can accept the 72-hour initial notice in writing, we can sign off quickly and put the envelope in DocuSign.

—Olga
Director, Security Engineering — Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_breach_compromise_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks — we've reviewed the compromise language and can accept the 72-hour initial notification as long as the cooperation clause includes: (1) an explicit escalation contact list; (2) a commitment to provide non-privileged evidence within 10 business days where available; and (3) an explicit statement that cost recovery may apply for extraordinary forensic exports.

We will not accept a blanket "reasonable efforts" without the timelines above. That said, our GC is prepared to approve provided we get the DocuSign envelope by EOD 12/01 so our procurement team can complete signature by 12/03. Please send the envelope link and indicated signer order.
